key_insight: PRISM shows that fixed random nonlinear features can support competitive anomaly detection without neural weight optimization or pretrained representations.
engineering_relevance: PRISM provides a training-free neural baseline for testing whether learned representations add value in tabular anomaly detection and visual defect localization.
method: Map inputs through fixed random nonlinear neural features.
Score anomalies using Mahalanobis distance relative to normal-reference statistics.
Use PRISM-T for tabular detection and PRISM-V for dense visual localization.
evidence_signal: Across 47 ADBench datasets, PRISM-T achieved 86.4% mean AUROC (highest) and 65.9% mean AUPRC (second-highest); across 27 MVTec AD and VisA categories, PRISM-V achieved 90.4% image-level and 96.4% pixel-level mean AUROC.
watch_item: No neural weight optimization does not mean no fitting: normal-reference statistics must still be estimated, making reference quality and covariance stability implementation concerns.
paper_title: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
